assumptions.condition: The selection response depends on assignment \(Z\) only through received treatment \(D\), with potential responses \(S_0\) and \(S_1\).
The ordinal outcome response depends on assignment \(Z\) only through received treatment \(D\), with potential responses \(Y_0\) and \(Y_1\).

standard.name: instrument exclusion for the selected outcome

novel.justification: The restriction permits both entry and exit responses within every covariate cell while limiting only the less prevalent direction after aggregation. It is interpretable in programs where employment or utilization can rise for most compliers but fall for a smaller subgroup, and it nests covariate-dependent one-sided selection at \(\delta_S=0\).

definitions.name: Observed arm-state masses
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(z,d\in\{0,1\}\), and \(w\in\mathcal V\), set \(q^z_{xdw}=p_xP(D=d,V=w\mid X=x,Z=z)\).

definitions.name: Diagonal residual margins
definitions.construction: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(w\in\mathcal V\), choose \(0\le d_{xdw}\le\min\{q^0_{xdw},q^1_{xdw}\}\) and set \(u_{xw}=q^0_{x0w}-d_{x0w}\), \(r_{xw}=q^1_{x0w}-d_{x0w}\), \(v_{xw}=q^1_{x1w}-d_{x1w}\), and \(s_{xw}=q^0_{x1w}-d_{x1w}\). Impose \(\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}u_{xw}=\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}v_{xw}=c_x\) and \(\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}r_{xw}=\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}s_{xw}=f_x\).

definitions.name: Selected complier margins
definitions.construction: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), set \(U_x=\sum_{i=0}^{K-1}u_{xi}\) and \(V_x=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}v_{xj}\); then the selection-response masses associated with survivor mass \(h_x\) are \(a_x=U_x-h_x\) and \(b_x=V_x-h_x\).

definitions.name: Variable-mass ordinal threshold cuts
definitions.construction: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), define \(B_{xk}=\sum_{i>k}u_{xi}+\sum_{j\le k}v_{xj}\) for \(k=-1,\ldots,K-1\), and \(G_{xk}=\sum_{i<k}u_{xi}+\sum_{j>k}v_{xj}\) for \(k=0,\ldots,K\), with all sums restricted to \(i,j\in\mathcal Y\) and empty sums equal to zero.

definitions.name: Orientation-specific threshold-cut polytope
definitions.construction: For \(o\in\mathcal O\), let \(Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\) contain exactly the arrays \((d,u,v,r,s,(c_x)_x,(f_x)_x,(h_x)_x,(n_x)_x)\) satisfying \(\text{def:diagonal-residuals}\), \(\max\{0,U_x+V_x-c_x\}\le h_x\le\min\{U_x,V_x\}\), \(0\le n_x\le h_x\), \(n_x\ge h_x-B_{xk}\) for every \(k=-1,\ldots,K-1\), \(n_x\le G_{xk}\) for every \(k=0,\ldots,K\), \(\sum_x f_x\le\delta_D\), and \(\sum_x\{o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x\}\le\delta_S\sum_x c_x\). Prefix-sum recurrences for \(u\) and \(v\) give an equivalent rational extended formulation with \(O(mK)\) variables, constraints, and nonzero coefficients.

definitions.name: Denominator-safe endpoint linear programs
definitions.construction: For a matrix representation \(Q_o=\{z:Az\le b,Ez=e,z\ge0\}\) with \(H=\eta z\) and \(N=\nu z\), minimize or maximize \(\nu y\) subject to \(Ay\le b\lambda\), \(Ey=e\lambda\), \(y\ge0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\eta y=1\).

definitions.name: Finite-sample multinomial primitive region
definitions.construction: Let \(M_0=4m(K+1)\), set \(\varepsilon_n=\sqrt{\log(2M_0/\alpha)/(2n_{\rm samp})}\), and define \(\mathcal P_n=\{\pi'\in\Delta^{M_0-1}:|\pi'_j-\widehat\pi_j|\le\varepsilon_n\text{ for all }j\}\).

definitions.name: Projected outer confidence surface
definitions.construction: For every \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\in\mathcal B\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_D,\delta_S)=\bigcup_{\pi'\in\mathcal P_n}\Theta_I(q(\pi');\delta_D,\delta_S)\), where candidates with zero conditioning mass are omitted and \(q(\pi')\) is obtained by the arm-conditioning map in \(\text{def:observed-masses}\).

definitions.name: Canonical adjacency-and-stratification handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\mathsf A_{\rm chart}\) by starting from an exact optimal basis at an algebraic sample budget, traversing adjacent canonical optimality regions with lexicographic primal--dual tie breaking, quotienting bases that induce the same unperturbed rational endpoint, and recursing on determinant-zero, feasibility-boundary, orientation-tie, and denominator-zero strata while retaining dual and full-law lift certificates.

statements.statement: Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\), nonnegative selected complier margins \((u_{xi})_{i\in\mathcal Y}\) and \((v_{xj})_{j\in\mathcal Y}\), and \(h_x\) satisfying \(\max\{0,U_x+V_x-c_x\}\le h_x\le\min\{U_x,V_x\}\). The attainable strict-benefit masses are exactly \([\max\{0,h_x-\min_kB_{xk}\},\min\{h_x,\min_kG_{xk}\}]\), equivalently exactly the values satisfying all inequalities in \(\text{def:orientation-polytope}\). Every such value is attained by a selected-selected coupling that can be completed with missing categories to the prescribed complier margins.
statements.justification: Threshold cuts replace \(K^2\) selected-selected coupling arcs by \(O(K)\) inequalities while retaining exact attainability for variable survivor mass.
statements.gap: Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen derive symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds without a latent selection-defined denominator; the variable-mass partial matching and missing-category completion are absent there.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies the compact ordinal component required to compute Job Corps wage-bin and Oregon utilization-bin benefit bounds.

statements.statement: For every observed mass array \(q\) and budget pair \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\in\mathcal B\), the projection of all laws \(P\in\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) inducing \(q\) onto \((d,h,n)\) is exactly \(\bigcup_{o\in\mathcal O}Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\). Every point of every branch \(Q_o\) lifts to a full response law inducing the same \(q\), with the displayed \(h_x\) and \(n_x\). Each branch admits a rational extended formulation with \(O(mK)\) variables, constraints, and nonzero coefficients.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it converts a nonconvex full response-law problem into exact linear-size branches without losing any compatible law or projected point.
statements.gap: Dong and Heiler maintain treatment monotonicity and within-cell one-sided selection for a mean target, Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen omit post-treatment selection, and Bartalotti, Kédagni, and Possebom use latent-index treatment selection and a monotone-selection refinement that exclude, respectively, treatment defiers and within-cell opposing selection responses. None contains this joint projection or reverse lift.
statements.consumer: It makes the survivor-complier ordinal-benefit robustness surface exactly computable for the Job Corps and Oregon encouragement designs.

statements.statement: If \(\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\) is nonempty, then it is the attained closed interval \([L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S),U(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)]\), even when the infimum of \(H\) over compatible positive-denominator laws is zero. For each unscreened orientation, the two endpoints are obtained by the normalized programs in \(\text{def:normalized-endpoint-program}\); after the observable residual-capacity direction screen, at most \(2^{r_{\rm amb}+1}\) rational linear programs are required.
statements.justification: The result handles vanishing denominators without trimming the model and turns an exponential branch count into a data-adaptive exact count.
statements.gap: Linear-fractional response-law formulations are known, but no adjacent result proves endpoint attainment and scalar connectedness for this disjunctive minority-budget class.
statements.consumer: Applied researchers obtain one interpretable sharp interval at every sensitivity pair, with no arbitrary lower cutoff on the always-selected-complier share.

statements.statement: Every finite sharp endpoint in \(\{L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S),U(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\}\) is attained by a compatible full response law whose legal observational-arc representation has at most \(m\{4(K+1)-1\}+2\) positive arcs. Such a law can be extracted from a reduced optimum by exposing the endpoint face, maximizing \(H\) on that face, and selecting a vertex.
statements.justification: Sharpness is empirically auditable only when endpoint allocations can be reported as finite latent-law certificates.
statements.gap: Generic bound solvers certify an objective value but need not return a sparse, positive-denominator full-law lift for the selected principal stratum.
statements.consumer: Endpoint certificates let analysts diagnose which compliance, selection, and outcome types drive robustness conclusions in Job Corps and Oregon.

statements.statement: For rational \(q\), the budget domain \(\mathcal B\) has a finite semialgebraic stratification, including its singular and lower-dimensional strata, on each nonempty stratum of which \(L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\) and \(U(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\) equal specified rational functions of \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\); every remaining stratum is labeled either model-infeasible or target-empty and carries an exact certificate.
statements.justification: The entire sensitivity chart, rather than a grid of unrelated optimizations, is the object needed for transparent robustness analysis.
statements.gap: Masten and Poirier obtain analytic frontiers in a smooth two-relaxation model; existing parametric-program algorithms do not directly provide this disjunctive ratio chart with all boundary labels.
statements.consumer: The chart supports exact comparative statics and reproducible breakdown reporting without grid interpolation.

statements.statement: For every \(t\in[0,1]\), the robust region \(\mathcal R_t\) is downward closed in both budgets and has a finite piecewise-algebraic boundary obtained from the chart in \(\text{thm:finite-rational-charts}\). The chart separately labels the falsification boundary, the positive-\(H\) target-existence boundary, and the conclusion boundary \(L=t\).
statements.justification: Separating incompatibility, an empty target stratum, and failure of the benefit conclusion prevents three substantively different robustness failures from being conflated.
statements.gap: Masten and Poirier and Picchetti study breakdown frontiers where the target remains defined across the maintained region; survivor-complier mass introduces a distinct existence frontier.
statements.consumer: An analyst can report the weakest joint monotonicity relaxations under which a stated minimum fraction of always-selected compliers benefits.

statements.statement: Under \(n_{\rm samp}\) independent draws of \((X,Z,D,V)\) with joint multinomial law \(\pi\), the primitive region \(\mathcal P_n\) satisfies \(P_{\pi}(\pi\in\mathcal P_n)\ge1-\alpha\). Consequently, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), \(\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\subseteq\mathcal C_n(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) simultaneously for every \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\in\mathcal B\) at which the population target exists.
statements.justification: One primitive coverage event protects every budget, orientation tie, and endpoint switch without gridwise multiplicity corrections.
statements.gap: Huang et al. give pointwise asymptotic inference for complete outcomes, while Kaido et al. and Cho--Russell give asymptotic projection methods; none gives this finite-sample whole-surface outer guarantee.
statements.consumer: The theorem provides an honest default uncertainty display for sensitivity surfaces before design-specific refinements for the Job Corps and Oregon samples.

statements.statement: If \(\delta_D=\delta_S=0\), the branches reduce to no-defier covariate-dependent one-sided selection. If additionally \(S_0=S_1=1\) almost surely among compliers, then \(H=\sum_xc_x\) and \(\Theta_I\) reduces to the standard sharp ordinal strict-benefit interval obtained from the complier marginal distributions; for \(K=2\), its cellwise numerator inequalities reduce to \(\max\{0,h_x-u_{x1}-v_{x0}\}\le n_x\le\min\{h_x,u_{x0},v_{x1}\}\).
statements.justification: The reductions verify that the joint sensitivity geometry collapses to known no-defier and complete-selection ordinal bounds in standard special cases.
statements.gap: The special cases are settled by Dong--Heiler and ordinal coupling results; the contribution is the exact interpolation when both monotonicities fail.
statements.consumer: These reductions provide implementation unit tests and interpretable baseline points for applied sensitivity charts.

statements.statement: Can the handle \(\mathsf A_{\rm chart}\) be completed into a degeneracy-safe exact algorithm that emits all feasible full-dimensional rational endpoint charts, all singular and lower-dimensional strata, all model-infeasible and target-empty labels, and sparse liftable endpoint certificates, with total bit complexity bounded by \(\operatorname{poly}(\ell_{\rm in},m,K)(M_{\rm out}+1)\) and with no uncharged exponential enumeration of rejected bases?
statements.justification: A finite all-bases construction does not certify scalable symbolic sensitivity analysis; the open theorem asks for complexity charged to the actual econometric output.
statements.gap: Columbano, Fukuda, and Jones charge work to perturbed sufficient-matrix critical domains, and Jones, Kerrigan, and Maciejowski output a nonoverlapping perturbed optimizer; neither guarantee matches the unperturbed stratified ratio-chart output.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would make exact whole-surface reporting practical when many covariate cells remain orientation-ambiguous.

sampling_model.design: A binary instrument \(Z\) randomized conditionally on finite-support \(X\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of \((X,Z,D,V)\) for the finite-sample coverage theorem; identification itself is a population-law statement.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary received treatment \(D=D_Z\) with all four compliance types permitted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Observed arm-state masses \(q\) are multinomial functionals; the baseline confidence surface projects a simultaneous primitive region and does not require a smooth endpoint estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Provides partial identification and inference for treatment effects with endogenous treatment and weak sample-selection monotonicity.
Expands sharp ordinal-benefit bounds to observational settings and imperfect randomized trials.
Derives uniformly sharp bounds for marginal treatment effects among always-observed individuals in a latent-index treatment model, with tighter bounds under monotone sample selection.
Derives nonparametric average-effect bounds under sample selection and noncompliance.
Derives breakdown frontiers for average effects and the proportion benefiting under two assumption relaxations.
Derives LATE and average-effect bounds under joint relaxations of independence and monotonicity.
Constructs an output-sensitive polyhedral decomposition for sufficient-matrix multiparametric complementarity problems.
Uses lexicographic perturbation to obtain a unique continuous optimizer over nonoverlapping regions.
Its confidence interval procedure for the fraction benefiting is pointwise consistent.
Provides uniformly asymptotically valid calibrated-projection confidence intervals.
Provides uniform asymptotic inference using randomly perturbed linear-program value functions.

tldr: Random assignment can coexist with endogenous receipt and outcomes observed only in a post-treatment selected sample. The target is the probability of strict ordinal benefit among always-selected treatment compliers when both treatment monotonicity and selection monotonicity can fail. A defier-share budget and an aggregate minority-selection budget generate an exact finite union of orientation-specific, linear-size rational threshold-cut polytopes. A reverse construction lifts every projected point to a full response law, yielding attained sharp endpoints without a uniform survivor-mass lower bound, exact pointwise computation, finite rational sensitivity charts, distinct falsification and breakdown labels, and simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage. The genuinely open computational question is an output-sensitive chart enumerator that remains complete on degenerate and lower-dimensional strata.

project_justification.gap: Published selected-complier mean and marginal-treatment-effect bounds either maintain treatment monotonicity through a no-defier or latent-index model or tighten through one-sided selection, while published ordinal-benefit bounds under imperfect compliance omit truncation by selection. Existing two-assumption breakdown frontiers do not confront a latent principal-stratum denominator that can vanish.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied model permits treatment defiers and both opposing selection responses, constrains their prevalence through two interpretable budgets, and asks for an ordinal individual-benefit probability within the always-selected complier stratum.
project_justification.fill: The exact projection-and-lifting theorem reduces the compatible full laws to orientation-indexed threshold-cut polytopes of linear extended size. The induced endpoint and frontier theorems give a complete two-budget robustness object with certificates and finite-sample outer coverage.

related_work: Dong and Heiler (2026) provide the closest setup and writing model: assignment affects endogenous receipt, outcomes are selected, and the intensive-margin complier population is substantively examined in Job Corps and Oregon. Their sharp target is a mean under treatment monotonicity and covariate-dependent one-sided selection, so their trimming construction informs but does not subsume the joint-violation ordinal ratio. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) provide the closest identification technique for strict ordinal benefit: finite response functions and symbolic sharp optimization. Their framework has no post-treatment selection variable or selection-defined principal stratum; their Discussion instead identifies bootstrap inference and efficient incorporation of continuous covariates as extensions. Bartalotti, Kédagni, and Possebom (2023) derive uniformly sharp marginal-treatment-effect bounds for always-observed individuals under a latent-index treatment model. Their latent-index treatment rule excludes treatment defiers, while their tighter monotone-sample-selection result excludes the within-cell opposing selection responses permitted by the minority budget here. Chen and Flores (2015) jointly analyze noncompliance and sample selection for always-employed complier means under monotonicity and mean dominance. Masten and Poirier (2020) motivate a complete two-assumption conclusion-first chart; Picchetti (2026) shows how a defier-share coordinate enters an IV breakdown analysis. Columbano, Fukuda, and Jones (2009) and Jones, Kerrigan, and Maciejowski (2007) inform the adjacency and lexicographic-degeneracy handle, but their output objects differ from unperturbed disjunctive rational endpoint charts. Huang et al. (2019), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Cho and Russell (2024) inform constrained and projection inference; the proposed baseline guarantee is instead a conservative finite-sample projection of one simultaneous multinomial region.
technical_internal_limitation: The presolve evidence supports finite exact all-bases chart enumeration but not output-sensitive complexity. The early kill test must reproduce the explicit binary surface \(L(d,s)=\max\{0,(0.05-d-s(0.20+d))/(0.15+d-s(0.20+d))\}\) and \(U(d,s)=(0.05+d)/\max\{0.10,0.15-s(0.20+d)\}\) on \(d\in[0,0.05]\), \(s\in[0,1/2]\), together with the opposite-orientation witness and a vanishing-denominator example. It must emit equality strata, empty-target labels, endpoint full-law certificates, and an audit showing that rejected bases do not hide exponential work. Failure triggers a computational-kernel pivot; it does not invalidate the projection theorem or pointwise endpoint algorithm.
honest_scope: The projection, sharpness, connectedness, sparse-attainment, finite-chart, frontier, and coverage claims are theorem obligations, not established results. The output-sensitive enumerator is deliberately exposed as the first-class open question. No strongly polynomial algorithm, polynomial bound on the number of orientations or charts, root-\(n\) regular endpoint inference at ties, or empirical reanalysis is claimed. Under complete selection and zero budgets, the target reduces to the known ordinal complier-benefit bounds.

seed_details.title: Sharp two-budget survivor-complier ordinal-benefit surface
seed_details.anchor_read: The source file was read at the Introduction, Assumptions 2.1--2.2, Proposition 2.1 and its supplementary sharpness proof, and the concluding remarks. The first changed proof step is the identification of one complier selection mixture: treatment defiers make both complier margins latent, while a positive minority budget prevents either selection-response type from being deleted.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining ordinal benefit, always-selected compliers, defier-share sensitivity, selection-monotonicity sensitivity, and breakdown surfaces found separate mean-selection and ordinal-benefit results but no exact joint target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Dong and Heiler because their weak selection monotonicity already permits the direction to vary with covariates.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their within-cell direction is one-sided and treatment monotonicity is maintained; the proposed law permits both selection directions in a cell and treatment defiers, making the complier margins, survivor denominator, and ordinal coupling jointly latent.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is not a generic response-type linear program: it requires an explicit linear-size threshold-cut projection, both lifting directions, an attained ratio image, and a two-coordinate sensitivity frontier.

seed_details.title: Degeneracy-safe output-sensitive rational chart enumeration
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, graph-search algorithm, lexicographic perturbation construction, post-processing result, Theorems 6.1--6.2, and Conclusion were read. The first changed proof step is neighborhood completeness: the econometric programs have a finite disjunction, a budget in a constraint coefficient, ratio objectives after homogenization, and output obligations on singular and empty-target strata.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search paired output-sensitive parametric optimization with rational partial-identification surfaces, Charnes--Cooper programs, singular strata, and full-law certificates. The closest results cover sufficient-matrix parametric complementarity or perturbed multiparametric linear programs, not this output specification.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Columbano, Fukuda, and Jones by converting each homogenized endpoint linear program into a parametric complementarity problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their output-sensitive accounting explores perturbed critical domains under a sufficient-matrix representation and then discards lower-dimensional artifacts; it does not charge work to unperturbed rational-value charts, singular strata, empty-target labels, or disjunctive full-law certificates.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is an algorithm-and-complexity theorem with a named certificate output, not a claim that a finite all-bases enumeration is output-sensitive.

seed_details.title: Finite-sample outer coverage of the complete sensitivity surface
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, the stochastic-optimization null, Theorems 1--4 and their proof architecture, and Discussion were read. The first changed proof step is inversion at a single complete-outcome benefit value: the new confidence object must cover a continuum of budgets, changing orientation branches, feasibility labels, and a possibly vanishing principal-stratum denominator.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing missing outcomes, noncompliance, fraction benefiting, simultaneous surface coverage, and finite-sample multinomial projection found pointwise asymptotic benefit intervals and asymptotic projection methods, but no finite-sample whole-surface guarantee for the joint principal-stratum model.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from any simultaneous multinomial confidence region by the deterministic mapping theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The coverage implication is simple only after an exact, denominator-safe projection has been proved; the research content is the surface-valued projection with infeasible and empty-target labels, while computationally efficient projection remains open.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is explicitly conservative outer coverage rather than an efficiency or exact-size claim.

seed_details.title: Separate falsification, target-existence, and conclusion breakdown frontiers
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorem 1 on sharp distributional-effect bounds, the frontier construction, and Conclusion were read. The first changed proof step is the maintained existence of the target: the survivor-complier denominator may be zero even when the observed law is compatible.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found breakdown frontiers for treatment-effect distributions and LATE sensitivity, but no chart separating model feasibility, positive principal-stratum mass, and a survivor-complier benefit conclusion.
seed_details.red_team: A breakdown frontier is merely a level set of the lower endpoint.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection defeats this as a separate kernel once the sharp surface is available; the three labels remain a theorem-level corollary of the selected seed.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped as a standalone seed because its strongest content is absorbed by the selected projection theorem.

seed_details.title: Joint-violation bounds for the full distribution of ordinal gains
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Section 3.2, Theorem 2, Results 3--4, the canonical response-function construction, and Discussion were read. The first changed proof step is their finite response-function optimization: conditioning on always-selected compliers makes both the numerator coupling and its normalizing mass endogenous to latent compliance-selection allocations.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for gain-threshold distributions among selected compliers under defiers found ordinal benefit bounds without selection and selected-mean bounds without gain distributions.
seed_details.red_team: Replace the strict-benefit edge set by \(j-i>t\) in the same transport problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: For each fixed threshold that replacement is feasible, but a coherent full distribution requires cross-threshold compatibility and a common latent law, which is materially harder than separate endpoint calculations.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The common-law compatibility requirement avoids padding the paper with independent scalar linear programs, but feasibility is too uncertain for the first version.

seed_details.title: Sharp joint surfaces for no-harm and relative treatment effect
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, definitions of benefit, no harm and relative treatment effect, Sections 3.1--3.3, and Discussion were read. The first changed proof step is again the response-function marginal map, now intersected with a latent always-selected-complier stratum and two violation budgets.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact joint selection--defier target was unoccupied, but each alternative estimand uses the same latent projection once that projection is available.
seed_details.red_team: The new targets are mechanical changes of edge weights in the selected seed's polytope.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for a standalone proposal, so these estimands are reserved as extensions rather than counted as the kernel.

seed_details.title: Frontier comparing aggregate and cellwise violations of selection monotonicity
seed_details.anchor_read: The covariate-dependent selection-direction setup, classification-margin regularity, Theorem 5.1, applications, and Conclusion were read. The first changed proof step is sign classification: an aggregate minority budget permits both signs within a covariate cell and transfers slack across cells.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found covariate-varying one-sided selection and unconditional one-sided selection, but no law-level comparison frontier between cellwise and aggregate minority restrictions.
seed_details.red_team: The aggregate model is simply a weaker assumption and therefore produces wider bounds by set inclusion.
seed_details.rebuttal: Exact coincidence and divergence frontiers could be nontrivial, but no observed-primitive frontier emerged that was independent of the selected surface calculation.

seed_details.title: Observable orientation screening with minimal branch complexity
seed_details.anchor_read: The critical-domain adjacency theorem, symbolic Chebyshev-center tests, degeneracy section, and complexity theorem were read. The first changed proof step is discovery of all relevant branches: orientation branches can be ruled out through observed defier-capacity intervals before any endpoint optimization.
seed_details.destination_search: No source was found that characterizes the smallest data-certified orientation family for a principal-stratum sensitivity program.
seed_details.red_team: The screen is only interval arithmetic before enumerating \(2^m\) orientations.
seed_details.rebuttal: Necessity of a branch-minimal screen would be substantive, but the available derivation establishes only a safe screen; it is retained as a computational theorem rather than the headline.

seed_details.title: Orthogonal inference for disjunctive ratio endpoints
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, linear-program value formulation, Theorem 3.1, Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, and Conclusion were read. The first changed proof step is stochastic perturbation of one linear-program value: the proposed endpoint is a minimum over orientations of linear-fractional values and is undefined on zero-denominator branches.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found perturbed linear-program inference and orthogonal inference for smooth Lee-type endpoints, but no regular influence function uniformly across orientation ties and denominator disappearance.
seed_details.red_team: Randomly perturb every branch and bootstrap the minimum of their value functions.
seed_details.rebuttal: A fixed nonvanishing perturbation changes the sharp surface, while a vanishing perturbation must handle branch appearance and disappearance; no credible uniform regularity argument survived the scan.

threads.settled: Sharp mean intensive-margin complier bounds under treatment monotonicity and covariate-dependent one-sided selection, with efficient orthogonal inference.
threads.boundary: No treatment defiers, no within-cell opposing selection types, and no ordinal strict-benefit target.

threads.settled: Sharp symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds for imperfect randomized studies, including specifications with and without no-defiers.
threads.boundary: No post-treatment selection variable and no survivor-complier denominator; the Discussion instead identifies bootstrap inference and efficient incorporation of continuous covariates as extensions.

threads.settled: Uniformly sharp marginal-treatment-effect bounds for always-observed individuals in a latent-index treatment model, including tighter bounds under monotone sample selection.
threads.boundary: The latent-index treatment rule excludes treatment defiers, and the monotone-selection refinement excludes within-cell opposing selection responses.

threads.settled: Mean-effect bounds for always-employed compliers under noncompliance, sample selection, monotonicity, and mean dominance.
threads.boundary: No simultaneous monotonicity failures and no ordinal individual-benefit functional.

threads.settled: Two-coordinate LATE sensitivity to defiers and instrument dependence, with a breakdown frontier and bootstrap inference.
threads.boundary: The second coordinate relaxes independence rather than selection monotonicity, and the outcome is not truncated by selection.

literature_map.occupation_check: The exact target--method pair is unoccupied in the inspected literature: strict ordinal benefit among always-selected compliers under both a defier-share budget and an aggregate opposing-selection-type budget.
literature_map.subsumption_check: No closer paper, including the latent-index always-observed analysis of Bartalotti, Kédagni, and Possebom, supplies the orientation-union projection, variable-survivor threshold cuts, or a full-law lift under both treatment defiers and opposing selection responses.

threads.settled: Output-sensitive critical-domain traversal for sufficient-matrix multiparametric complementarity problems, with lexicographic degeneracy handling.
threads.boundary: The output is a perturbed polyhedral solution cover, not an unperturbed rational value chart with singular strata and certificates.

threads.settled: Lexicographic perturbation gives a unique continuous optimizer on nonoverlapping regions for degenerate multiparametric linear programs.
threads.boundary: The guarantee does not preserve every equality stratum or charge computation only to the econometric value-chart output.

threads.settled: Complete two-dimensional sensitivity frontiers are an econometric reporting object.
threads.boundary: Their frontier is analytic and smooth enough for functional methods, not the output of disjunctive parametric ratio programs.

literature_map.occupation_check: No exact rational, degeneracy-safe, output-sensitive enumerator with the specified lower-dimensional and lift-certificate output was found.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The sufficient-matrix and fixed multiparametric-linear-program results do not directly cover coefficient-varying disjunctive Charnes--Cooper systems.

threads.settled: Pointwise-consistent test-inversion intervals for one ordinal fraction-benefiting parameter in a complete-outcome randomized trial.
threads.boundary: Missing outcomes are expressly left for future work, and coverage is neither finite-sample nor simultaneous over a sensitivity continuum.

threads.settled: Uniformly asymptotically valid calibrated projection for subvectors of moment-inequality parameters.
threads.boundary: The guarantee is asymptotic and does not label a continuum of infeasible or zero-denominator programs.

threads.settled: Uniform asymptotic confidence sets from randomly perturbed linear-program value functions.
threads.boundary: A fixed perturbation yields an outer limiting set and does not preserve the exact disjunctive surface.

threads.settled: Root-\(n\) efficient inference for two smooth sharp mean-bound functionals away from classification and trimming degeneracies.
threads.boundary: The assumptions exclude the orientation ties and vanishing denominator that define the new surface's difficult strata.

literature_map.occupation_check: No finite-sample confidence object simultaneously covering every budget-indexed survivor-complier benefit set was found.
literature_map.subsumption_check: Primitive multinomial-region projection gives a different, conservative guarantee and depends on the selected seed's exact law projection.
